newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: PRESIDENT DOUBTS GOV'T COMPENSATION PLAN.
newsitem.headline: PRESIDENT DOUBTS GOV'T COMPENSATION PLAN.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas on Wednesday said that he had serious doubts about the government's plan to compensate depositors who lost their savings in 1990-1991.
"We must find realistic instead of mystic ways to compensate those who lost their savings," Brazauskas said in an interview with Reuters.
"This has been an unresolved problem since independence," he added.

The government last week said it planned to present a draft law to parliament to compensate depositors who lost their savings through confiscation from the Soviet era savings bank and hyper-inflation.
The government says the plan will cost three billion litas and will be paid for from the sale of state property and enterprises which have an estimated value of over four billion litas.
Brazauskas said he did not think it was right to "sell national assets which belong to everyone to compensate one group of people".
"This issue must not be turned into political play ahead of the (presidential and local) election campaigns," he said.
